findings.issue: `pkill -f 'srvx serve'` matched the invoking shell's own command line and killed the session's command (exit 143); the mistake was repeated at trace.md:741 with a different self-matching pattern ('api/server.mjs'), costing ~4 turns.
findings.suggestion: Kill background servers by recorded PID (the script already wrote /tmp/app.pid, /tmp/api.pid) or use a non-self-matching pattern like '[s]rvx serve'.

findings.issue: Killing the npm parent left the srvx child alive, so the restart hit EADDRINUSE and the agent nearly attributed the unstyled page to a CSS bug before checking ps and the server log.
findings.suggestion: Start background servers with their own PID file (exec the srvx process directly rather than via npm) or kill the process group, and check `ps`/port status before re-launching.

findings.issue: Curl probe aimed at port 3000 while the app had been started on PORT=3100, producing a confusing 000 result.
findings.suggestion: Probe the port the start command actually used, or default the dev-loop server to PORT=3000 to match the spec.

findings.issue: Two consecutive read calls failed schema validation by passing 'file' instead of 'path'.
findings.suggestion: Use the correct parameter name; these were pure wasted calls.

findings.issue: Attempted a PIL-based image crop without checking the module was installed, and the follow-up turn searching for convert/magick also found nothing.
findings.suggestion: Check tool availability first (`python3 -c 'import PIL'`) or skip the crop — the full screenshots were already readable.

findings.issue: Inspection command grepped nonexistent paths (/app, /aws, /cloud) due to apparent path typos, returning nothing.
findings.suggestion: Use the verified working path (/home/agent/work) in the same command instead of guessing variants.

summary: A disciplined, front-loaded session: it derived test expectations from the data, pinned current TanStack Start practices by scaffolding the official template and reading the docs, and got the build and all 54 acceptance tests passing on the first attempt. Verification then went beyond the tests with design-screenshot comparisons, tsc, and a final full-suite run after the last edits. The only real drag was background-process management (a self-killing pkill loop and an orphaned server), which cost roughly ten turns without ever threatening correctness.
